title: I built a stickman beat 'em up. Here's the new trailer
author: Dazzling_Abalone_864
selftext:
Hey r/AIGameDev! I’ve been heads-down building **Hard Counter: Stickman Fight**, a rooftop beat 'em up centered on dynamic reaction-based combat (read telegraph signals, counter, and chain attacks across 30 waves).

Since this sub focuses on solo pipelines, tool workflows, and technical dev mechanics, I wanted to share the new trailer along with a breakdown of how the combat state machine works and a few code/pipeline hurdles I ran into along the way.

Enemies telegraph with sparks over their heads. Blue means counter, red means a blade (evade), yellow means a gun (dodge the shot). Read it right and you chain from one thug to the next. Land enough clean hits and you unlock brutal ground finishers: Leg Break, Arm Bar, Neck Snap, plus two-at-once counters like the Head Clash.  


It's in closed testing on Android, submitted to the App Store, and it's coming to Steam and (hopefully) Xbox. There's a free browser demo on itch if you want to try the combat: [https://inveighgames.itch.io/](https://inveighgames.itch.io/)  
  
I'd love feedback on the trailer.

You can go full screen in the settings menu.

SUB RULE 4 - How Ai was used - I had to rely heavily on precise **hitstop frames, localized camera shake curves**, and specific joint-angle snapping during finisher animations to convey heavy impact. Re-timing the leg break frame-data took about six iterations to feel truly mechanical. My virtual joystick had a frustrating bug where moving right registered as a slow walk instead of a sprint. The issue came down to how radial distance was calculated when a player's thumb dragged past the outer control ring, which registered as a *weaker* push vector. Fixing the radial normalization math took two days of debugging for what ended up being a single line of logic. Managing my platform-specific builds (Android, iOS, [itch.io](http://itch.io), Steam, and Xbox) as a solo developer is about 50% gameplay logic and 50% submission pipelines, entitlement setups, and API alignment. Automating build configurations per target platform saved a massive amount of technical overhead. If anyone has any questions feel free to let me know.
